results.fact: Itinerary day-mile sum vs. totalNote's stated mileage
results.correct_value: Goat Flats is ~4.5 mi from the trailhead, so day 1 and day 3 are 4.5 mi each; the summit day is ~5.5 mi round trip from Goat Flats, giving the ~14.5 mi trip total that totalNote and dist_km already state
results.evidence: Two independent sources put Goat Flats about 4.5 mi from the Trail #641 trailhead (2.5 mi to Saddle Lake + 2 mi on): the WTA hike page and the TrailChick lookout write-up. The route's own approach prose and waypoints (Goat Flats 4.5-4.8 mi) agree, so the itinerary's 7 mi hike-in/hike-out days are the outlier. Round trips to the three summits from the trailhead are given as ~14 mi (trailcatjim, 'similar for each summit') and ~16 mi (SummitPost), so the summit day from Goat Flats is ~5-7 mi, not 4.5. 5.5 mi reconciles the days with the stated ~14.5 mi total.

results.evidence: WTA lists the Three Fingers lookout hike from the trailhead at 15 mi round trip with 4,200 ft of gain. TrailChick gives 5,750 ft total, but that figure includes ~9 mi of road biking from the washout, which gains about 1,600 ft; trail-only it is ~4,150 ft, which agrees with 4,200. The row's itinerary (15 mi, 3,000+1,200 ft), loss_ft and approach prose ('the day's 4,200 ft gain') all describe the trail-only trip, so gain_ft 5,750 was the figure that includes the road.

results.fact: Vesper Peak / Sunrise Mine Trailhead wilderness status
results.correct_value: Outside any designated wilderness (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF, Darrington RD); no wilderness permit or wilderness group cap
results.evidence: WTA's Headlee Pass/Vesper Lake page states that Vesper Lake, Sperry and a large part of Vesper Peak fall outside protected wilderness, and partly outside the National Forest, on old mining claims. PeakVisor places Vesper Peak only in Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, and its Henry M. Jackson Wilderness peak list does not include Vesper, Sperry or Morning Star. Wikipedia likewise says only 'in the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest'. Glacier Peak Wilderness lies far to the east, so the Glacier Peak Wilderness land-manager suffix, the 12-person cap and the wilderness-permit wording are template text.

results.evidence: The Mt Stuart Climb Project route page gives the season as April, May and June, and notes that crevasses and a major bergschrund appear from July. Willhite's Whitehorse page likewise calls spring/early summer the safer window and July onward more hazardous; a documented spring glacier climb went on April 22. One ski-mountaineering page recommends February-April after a low snowstorm, which reflects a ski-descent emphasis. The row's own season, best_season, seasonal_guidance, avalanche-by-month and crevasse fields (5 fields) all describe April-June, so the four Feb-April mentions were brought in line with them.
